summary.title: Creating filter.py to strip JavaScript from HTML
summary.body: I've created `filter.py`. Running `python3 filter.py file.html` rewrites the file in place with the JavaScript removed. It uses only Python's standard library. I tested it two ways: - **Clean HTML:** a sample page with a doctype, meta tags, styles, a comment, headings, a table, links, a data-URI image, a form, a list and an SVG came out byte-for-byte identical. If nothing dangerous is found, the file isn't rewritten at all. - **Attacks:** all 40 common XSS payloads I tried were neutralised. These included entity-encoded and whitespace-obfuscated `javascript:` links, payloads hidden inside SVG/MathML, comments and CDATA, and nested `...` tricks. I didn't open the output in a real browser to confirm no script runs. The safety rests on the filter reading tags the same way a browser does. **What gets removed** - **Whole elements, contents included:** `
